what: Blue Owl Capital is an alternative asset manager. It lends to mid-sized companies, buys stakes in other private equity firms, and owns buildings leased to single corporate tenants, charging fees on the money it manages.
customers: Pension funds, insurers, sovereign wealth funds and wealthy individuals who commit capital for years at a time.
money: direct lending to companies private equity firms own
minority stakes in other alternative managers
net-lease property and data centre investments
moat: Management fees charged on capital locked up for a decade, which keeps earning whether markets rise or fall, unlike a fund that investors can leave at any time.
risks: Direct lending to private-equity-owned companies is untested through a deep recession
64 times reported earnings, because amortisation of past acquisitions depresses the accounting profit
opportunities: $1.5B of free cash flow against $95M of reported net income, so the cash generation is far stronger than it looks
Revenue grew from $824M to $2.9B in four years as assets under management climbed
Analysts see about 41% upside, and data centre lending has become a large new market
watch: Fee-paying assets under management and new capital raised each quarter.
